title: introduce-retrypolicy-compiler-and-stream-progress-unify-py-ts-go
author: Maya Lin
description:
Motivation: We continue to see duplicated token refreshes and inconsistent retry behavior across SDKs during high-throughput streaming and batched workloads. This PR introduces a small, language-agnostic RetryPolicy compiler and a lightweight streaming progress envelope to bring parity and observability to Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Goals: 1) Provide a declarative RetryPolicy format that compiles to runtime presets (hedged/hedged-with-backoff, fast-fail, conservative) so callers can pick documented semantics rather than hand-tuning numeric knobs. 2) Stabilize reauth handshake under stream reconnects to avoid thrash (single-flight refresh, backoff alignment). 3) Surface a StreamProgress envelope on async iterators/async generators that exposes token/offset hints and last-heartbeat timestamps for observability and more ergonomic client-side resumption. 4) Bump SDK versions and ship coordinated docs and examples.
Scope: - Add retry policy compiler modules and test vectors in each SDK.
- Add a small StreamProgress struct/type on iterator yields and a `with_progress` opt-in flag on streaming helpers.
- Centralize credential preflight and singleflight refresh in the shared auth shim used by all three SDKs (language-native implementations).
- Update README / migration guides and release notes.
Backwards compatibility: All new behavior is opt-in (new RetryPolicy config or with_progress flag). Existing defaults remain unchanged to avoid surprises in production.
